Friends can text home, check the weather and look things up through your phone when it has signal — up to %1$d MB of your data a day.
Friends can text home, check the weather and look things up through your phone when it has signal — with no daily limit.

Phones in your group link to each other directly over Bluetooth and WiFi — no tower, no router, no internet.

Every message is passed from phone to phone, so it can travel down a line of hikers or across a crowd, far beyond one phone's range.

Every phone carries the group's messages for 48 hours and fills in anyone who was away. Walk off, come back — the chat catches up on its own. What reaches your phone stays on it — even after you leave a group — until you delete it.

The ticks never lie: ◷ waiting for a phone in range, ✓ on its way, ✓✓ phones confirmed. Tap your own message to see exactly who has it.

The group chat is encrypted with a key made from the group's code: anyone who has the code can read it. A four-word code keeps out bystanders. Someone who spends about a week of graphics-card time once can afterwards work out any four-word code from the radio signal, and with it read the group chat — and an older three-word code in under an hour. Treat the group chat like a walkie-talkie, not a vault.

Private chats are end-to-end encrypted: only the two of you can read them, even though other phones carry them. Those phones can see who wrote to whom, and when — not what. To be sure who is on the other end, compare your security code with them (the private chat's menu → Verify security code). There is no forward secrecy: someone who records the radio and later gets the key out of a phone could read the private messages that were sent to it.

Chats are encrypted on the air, not on your phone: what reached it is kept as you see it, in Hopline's own storage.

Names aren't checked: anyone with the code can call themselves anything. When two people share a name, Hopline adds a short tag to tell them apart.

Whoever starts a group from now on is its first admin. Admins can make others admins, and can let only admins send messages — then phones with the latest Hopline don't show anyone else's group messages, while private chats still work. A phone still on an older Hopline doesn't know about admins and shows everything.

Since Hopline 2.4, phones on 2.3.1 or older can't join updated phones — everyone in the group needs the update. Private chats started fresh with it: the older ones are still there to read, and to keep talking you open the person again from People.
